title: Concept of equation
summary: Interpret an equation as a balance, test proposed solutions and recognise transformations that preserve the solution set.
objectives: Explain what it means for two expressions to be equal.
Test whether a value satisfies an equation by substitution.
Recognise that applying the same valid operation to both sides preserves equality.

blocks.text: An equation states that two expressions have the same value. A solution is a value of the variable that makes the statement true. The equals sign describes a relationship; it does not mean that a calculation must always follow it.

Substituting x = 4 gives 2(4) + 3 = 11, so 4 is a solution. An equation stays balanced when the same addition, subtraction, multiplication by a non-zero number, or division by a non-zero number is applied to both sides.

sections.title: Testing and transforming an equation

prompt.text: Show that x = 5 satisfies 3x - 4 = 11, then write an equivalent equation after adding 4 to both sides.

content.text: Because the two sides agree, x = 5 is a solution.

sections.verification_note: Substitution gives 11 = 11, and both equations have the same solution x = 5.

prompt.text: For 4x + 1 = 21, what value does the left-hand side have when x = 5?

feedback.text: Substituting x = 5 gives 4(5) + 1 = 21, matching the right-hand side.

blocks.text: Read the equals sign as a balance, test solutions by substitution, and change both sides with the same valid operation.
